transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Dora. I'm a clinical conversational agent, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have some questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise, such as gardening, one week after surgery. However, you should avoid strenuous exercise, lifting heavy objects, pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thank you. My next question is: when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I can only help with questions about your cataract surgery recovery. I don't have information about specific eye gels. However, if you were using any eye drops before your operation for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. If you have further questions about your eye gel, please contact your care team. Do you have any other questions for me?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. Do you have any other questions?
